why_how.text: Motorcycle riders have the same roadway rights and duties as other drivers, although they can be harder to see.
Give a motorcycle the full width of its lane so its rider has room to respond to other traffic.
Include motorcycles in mirror and blind-spot checks.
The handbook states that motorcycles require more stopping distance than cars and other passenger vehicles.
Do not assume a motorcycle will turn merely because its signal flashes, since the signal may not cancel automatically and may have been left on.
At low speed in ideal conditions, keep at least three seconds behind a motorcycle.
Use at least four seconds behind a motorcycle with higher speeds, heavy traffic, poor visibility, bad weather, unfamiliar surroundings or driver fatigue.
Expect a motorcyclist to change speed or lane position suddenly to avoid potholes, gravel, slippery surfaces, pavement seams, rails or grooved pavement.

why_how.text: A bicycle on the roadway is a vehicle and must travel with other traffic rather than against it.
Bicycle riders must obey signs, signals and pavement markings and follow the same road rules as motorized traffic.
Reduce speed when approaching or passing a bicycle rider.
Avoid sounding the horn close to a bicycle rider.
Pass a bicycle only when the maneuver can be completed safely.
Keep at least three feet between a motor vehicle and a bicycle.
Do not turn sharply across a bicycle rider's path or force the rider off the road.
Use particular care around bicycles on wet, sandy or gravel-covered roads because these conditions affect them more than motor vehicles.
Check for bicycle riders in the vehicle's path before backing.
Learn bicycle arm signals and, if a rider cannot signal, look for clues such as a head turn or shoulder check before a lane change.

why_how.text: Commercial vehicles are generally larger and less maneuverable than passenger cars.
Commercial vehicles have substantially larger blind spots than passenger vehicles.
Large commercial vehicles need more distance to stop and accelerate and more space to turn.
Give trucks and buses room for a wide right turn, which may start from a left lane to clear a curb or obstruction.
Never squeeze between a turning large vehicle and the curb; wait for its turn to finish before entering that space.
Stop behind intersection stop lines, which leave large vehicles additional turning room.
If uncertain about an approaching truck's or bus's speed, do not turn left across its path.
